title: Scientific Compilations: Bede, Pseudo-Ptolemy, Avicenna (Sloane MS 2030)
shelf_note: Physiognomy text (lips, cheeks, jaws, nostrils with animal analogies) in a scientific miscellany; consistent with the catalogue.
structure_note: Foliation numerals '100' (top) and '96' (bottom) both on the leaf; backsteps/repeats likely come from the two competing numberings, not a splice.

title: [Da fang guang fo hua yan jing] juan 41
shelf_note: Tangut block-print in folding (concertina) format, consistent with a Tangut Avatamsaka sutra; the stored text is what is wrong, not the catalogue.
structure_note: 15 pages, 11 translated. The page's own translation calls the work a 'lexicographical or phonetic manual', contradicting the title (Avatamsaka sutra, juan 41).

ocr_errors.image: five panels of about six columns each of varied Tangut characters, ~17 per column
ocr_errors.problem: the transcription is a loop of four or five code points, repeated block for block; none of it is the leaf's text

ocr_errors.image: a Tangut panel title followed by Chinese numeral 四 in the margin
ocr_errors.problem: Tangut margin characters rendered as Chinese characters

tr_errors.english: This section appears to be a lexicographical or phonetic manual ... [The structural arrangement of characters continues.] ×5
tr_errors.problem: no translation; a page description that wrongly calls a sutra a phonetic glossary, stored as the English

other.note: <gloss>categorized miscellaneous</gloss> on an invented reading 'Lèichú' — invented apparatus

pages.not_this_leaf_evidence: The stored Tangut is a handful of glyphs (𗦵𗰗𗽻𗰖) repeated, with whole columns duplicated, while the image shows some 30 columns of varied Tangut characters; the English then describes the page as a phonetic glossary, which the leaf of a sutra is not.

book_verdict: The transcription is invented (a loop of four glyphs) and the 'translation' is a wrong description of the page; nothing a reader is shown here comes from the leaf.

title: Excerptum decretorum, ca. 1350
shelf_note: Canon-law/sacramental extracts (baptism, confirmation) fit the title.

title: Plotini Libri XXVII posteriores Marsilio Ficino interprete
shelf_note: The leaf is Ficino's De vita III.21 (seven degrees of things, songs dedicated to Apollo), written as a commentary on Plotinus; plausible in a Ficino Plotinus volume.
structure_note: Stored page-num '48' while the leaf's foliation at bottom right looks like '108'; minor.

tr_errors.english: ...a certain form results—like a harmony endowed with the gifts of the stars—so from tones, first chosen according to the standard of the stars, then composed for their agreement among themselves, a common form is as it were made, and in it some celestial virtue arises.
tr_errors.problem: the last sentence of the English continues well past the end of the leaf (which stops at 'resultat cas'), supplying the rest of De vita III.21 that is not on this page

pages.not_this_leaf_evidence: The leaf's last line ends 'partem tum medicam tum astronomicam resultat cas', but the English goes on with 'like a harmony endowed with the gifts of the stars—so from tones, first chosen according to the standard of the stars ... some celestial virtue arises', text that belongs to the following page.

book_verdict: The transcription is good; the English is faithful until its last sentence, which runs on into the next page's text, and a clause is mis-tagged as a gloss.
